https://docs.openpo.st/development/relea.audience: Use bun run release -- prepare "<commit>" when you want to stop after the exact SHA has passed local and hosted checks. Finish later with bun run release -- promote <tag>. bun run release -- status compares the local SHA, candidate CI run, and public production revision.
https://docs.openpo.st/development/relea.boundary: The plan subcommand inventories every path changed since the latest release, plus staged, unstaged, and untracked work, before anything is written. config/release-surfaces.json assigns each maintained path to one or more release surfaces or a reasoned exemption; both release planning and CI fail when a new path has no owner. Pull-request CI uses that registry to run only affected runtime, site, browser, security, and image checks. Pushes to main still run the complete candidate matrix. The preflight subcommand checks the worktree, GitHub access, required workflows and deployment configuration, and current production readiness. bun run release -- check is the bounded local release gate: generated and type checks first, then formatting, lint, and non-browser unit tests in parallel, without production builds, Chromium component tests, browser suites, race tests, security scans, or Docker. The prod subcommand promotes CHANGELOG.md, runs the release, changelog, and provider-certification contracts locally, then commits and pushes main. GitHub CI is the correctness authority for the immutable candidate SHA, and the command waits for that matrix before creating a tag. Use bun run release -- check-full only when an explicit exhaustive local rehearsal is useful; it retains the build, race, security, browser, and production-image gates and the 24-hour exact-worktree stamp.

https://docs.openpo.st/operations/backup.boundary: The Hosted service makes daily Postgres dumps and a daily synchronized copy of Cloudflare R2 media in a root-owned directory on the application host. The directory is not public or application-served. The deployment configuration restricts its directory and newly created file modes, validates database compression before an atomic rename, disables SSH password and direct root login, and grants the named operator access through authorized SSH keys and sudo. Application users, support requests, and the OpenPost container do not receive backup-directory access.

https://docs.openpo.st/operations/contai.audience: The image's OCI health check calls /api/v1/health. This proves that the HTTP process is alive without turning a data-plane outage into a container restart loop. Traffic gates, deployment rollouts, and dependency-aware monitors call /api/v1/ready, which returns 503 when the database probe or required object-storage capability check fails. See Health Checks for the complete operator policy.
https://docs.openpo.st/operations/contai.boundary: The published OpenPost container image supports linux/amd64 only. The CI candidate build names that platform explicitly and restart-smokes that same image before it can be published. The maintained Dockerfile rejects non-amd64 targets. An ARM64 host must use amd64 emulation; a native ARM64 image requires an explicit downstream Dockerfile/source change and its own complete runtime smoke proof. OpenPost does not currently publish or claim support for a linux/arm64 image.

https://docs.openpo.st/operations/health.audience: Use this endpoint when you only need to know whether the HTTP process is alive. The published image's OCI health check and the maintained Compose file use it so a database outage does not turn into a container restart loop.
https://docs.openpo.st/operations/health.boundary: It returns 503 when OpenPost cannot run a database probe or the configured S3 bucket fails its bounded capability check.

https://docs.openpo.st/operations/logs.audience: Each HTTP request log includes both the requested path and the normalized matched route, such as /api/v1/publications/:id. The normalized route lets operators aggregate endpoint use without treating every resource ID as a separate path.
https://docs.openpo.st/operations/logs.boundary: Callers can set that header themselves, so the field is useful for deprecation and reachability review but is not an authentication, authorization, billing, or audit identity.

https://docs.openpo.st/operations/troubl.audience: Diagnose startup, database, media, provider, publishing, and delivery problems on a self-hosted OpenPost instance.
https://docs.openpo.st/operations/troubl.boundary: confirm there is only one primary OpenPost process using the database.

https://docs.openpo.st/operations/upgrad.audience: Read the release notes before every upgrade.
https://docs.openpo.st/operations/upgrad.boundary: A major version can require changes to your setup.

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/bluesky.audience: This page is for users connecting a Bluesky account.
https://docs.openpo.st/providers/bluesky.boundary: Bluesky video support is limited to one video attachment per post in OpenPost.

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/discord.audience: This page is for operators configuring Discord and users connecting a channel webhook.
https://docs.openpo.st/providers/discord.boundary: Discord webhooks can only send. They do not let OpenPost read a channel inbox, personal alerts, or direct messages.

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/faceboo.audience: This page is for operators configuring Facebook and users connecting a Page.
https://docs.openpo.st/providers/faceboo.boundary: Media URLs must be public HTTPS URLs.

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/instagr.audience: This page is for operators configuring Instagram and users connecting a professional account.
https://docs.openpo.st/providers/instagr.boundary: Instagram Business or Creator account connected to a Facebook Page

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/linkedi.audience: This page is for operators configuring LinkedIn and users connecting a member profile or Organization Page.
https://docs.openpo.st/providers/linkedi.boundary: OpenPost always offers the member profile returned by LinkedIn OpenID Connect. Organization Pages are an explicit operator opt-in because LinkedIn gates their permissions behind approved products:

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/mastodo.audience: This page is for operators configuring Mastodon and users connecting a custom or preconfigured instance.
https://docs.openpo.st/providers/mastodo.boundary: For custom instances: no static env entry is required, but the instance must be public HTTPS and allow app registration.

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/pintere.audience: This page is for operators reviewing Pinterest's certification boundary.
https://docs.openpo.st/providers/pintere.boundary: Pinterest is not publicly available in OpenPost.

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/telegra.audience: This page is for operators reviewing Telegram bot mode's certification boundary.
https://docs.openpo.st/providers/telegra.boundary: Telegram bot mode is not publicly available in OpenPost.

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/threads.audience: This page is for operators configuring Threads and users connecting an account.
https://docs.openpo.st/providers/threads.boundary: Threads supports text, single media, replies, and 2-20 item media carousels, but the media URL requirement makes deployment details matter.

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/tiktok.audience: This page is for operators configuring TikTok and users connecting an account.
https://docs.openpo.st/providers/tiktok.boundary: TikTok app lacks Content Posting API access or required scopes.

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/trouble.audience: Use this page when a provider connection, OAuth callback, media upload, or scheduled publish fails. Start by capturing a support snapshot:
https://docs.openpo.st/providers/trouble.boundary: It also includes the last 100 log lines with private data removed. It does not print full tokens or server secrets.

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/x.audience: This page is for operators configuring X and users connecting an account.
https://docs.openpo.st/providers/x.boundary: OpenPost currently uses X OAuth 1.0a end-to-end. Configure an app type that supports OAuth 1.0a user context and the callback URL above.

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/youtube.audience: This page is for operators configuring YouTube and users connecting a channel.
https://docs.openpo.st/providers/youtube.boundary: Test a live account before you rely on YouTube publishing, especially for app review, playlists, and thumbnails.

https://docs.openpo.st/reference/callbac.audience: This reference is for operators registering provider and identity callback URLs.
https://docs.openpo.st/reference/callbac.boundary: Mastodon uses the OOB flow by default and exchanges the pasted authorization code through /api/v1/accounts/mastodon/exchange. Only configure a normal Mastodon callback URL if you also override MASTODON_REDIRECT_URI.

https://docs.openpo.st/reference/cli.audience: openpost is a command-line client for the OpenPost social media scheduler. It talks to a running OpenPost instance over HTTPS, authenticates with a revocable API token, and exposes the most common posting, scheduling, account, and media workflows for use from scripts, CI, and power-user shells.
https://docs.openpo.st/reference/cli.boundary: This page is generated from the Cobra command tree. Do not edit it by hand.

https://docs.openpo.st/reference/surface.audience: This reference is for contributors and automation authors choosing an OpenPost client surface.
https://docs.openpo.st/reference/surface.boundary: all clients still use the same workspace authorization, validation, quota, and audit rules.

https://docs.openpo.st/self-hosting/.audience: Use these docs when you operate OpenPost on your own infrastructure.
https://docs.openpo.st/self-hosting/.boundary: A self-hosted operator handles deployment availability, user support, incidents, and operator-specific configuration.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/account-sec.audience: Open Settings → Personal → Security to manage your password, authenticator app, recovery codes, passkeys, linked sign-in identities, and active browser sessions. These settings belong to your login and apply in every workspace.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/account-sec.boundary: Web sign-in creates a persistent, HTTP-only session cookie that expires after seven days. OpenPost does not show a cosmetic “Remember me” option because there is currently one server-enforced lifetime. Sign out when you finish on a shared device. You can review and revoke active browser sessions from Settings → Personal → Security; revocation invalidates that session before its normal expiry.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/accounts.audience: Use this page when you want to connect or manage social accounts in a Workspace.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/accounts.boundary: If you cancel authorization or the provider cannot finish the connection, OpenPost returns to account management with a retry message. Refreshing or signing in again does not create a separate setup state; the Workspace setup guide reads current subscription, destination, first-composition, and Publication data.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/agent-assis.audience: An AI tool can prepare posts through MCP without seeing your social account keys.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/agent-assis.boundary: A person reviews the work before allowing a change.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/analytics.audience: Use this page when reviewing saved whole-account content results.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/analytics.boundary: Disabling Analytics stops future account, Rendition, and account-content collection for that account without deleting stored history or revoking provider authorization.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/auto-repost.audience: This page is for people configuring native same-network repost rules after publication.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/auto-repost.boundary: The source and target must be on the same network. OpenPost does not copy the post to a different network.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/communicati.audience: This page is for people reviewing and responding to saved engagement and messages in a Workspace.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/communicati.boundary: OpenPost checks social networks in the background and saves the results. Engagement at /inbox/engagement and Messages at /inbox/messages read saved data, so a slow or unavailable network does not block either page.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/composing-p.audience: This page is for people creating a Publication in the composer.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/composing-p.boundary: The Video Editor project, sources, and other exports remain in the disk workspace.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/destination.audience: This page is for people tailoring one Publication for each selected social account.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/destination.boundary: Open the settings beside a selected account to change its text and options. OpenPost only shows sections that apply: Content, Conversation, Distribution, Disclosure, and Media and accessibility.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/grow.audience: Use this page when reviewing account recommendations for growth.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/grow.boundary: Following a recommendation always requires Grow to remain enabled for that account and remains an explicit user action. OpenPost never follows an account automatically.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/image-edito.audience: You can return to local designs on the same device and export PNG, JPEG, or WebP files at any time. Save to OpenPost creates an account or uses your current account, uploads the local images, and copies the editable design into your workspace. The local copy remains available in the original browser.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/image-edito.boundary: The public editor works without sign-in and adds no watermark. Start with a social format, an OpenPost template, or a PNG, JPEG, or WebP image. Designs and imported images stay in that browser. Clearing site data, using private browsing, or letting the browser clear old data can remove local work.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/.audience: Use these docs to connect accounts, build or write account versions, schedule posts, track results, work with replies and messages, use the CLI, or grant an AI tool access through MCP.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/.boundary: Provider data, formats, and actions remain limited by the connected account and provider.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/media-libra.audience: This page is for people organizing reusable media and editor assets in a Workspace.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/media-libra.boundary: Disk-backed Video Editor projects are separate from Media and do not create hidden retention references.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/quick-cut.audience: Quick Cut removes ranges from one or more media files with the least processing possible.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/quick-cut.boundary: Quick Cut rejects plans that would silently drop unsupported subtitle, data, unknown-audio, or extra-video streams.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/recording.audience: Open /record to capture screen, camera, and microphone sources as separate synchronized files.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/recording.boundary: OpenPost requests screen, camera, or microphone access only after you start recording.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/scheduling.audience: The composer interprets dates and times in the workspace timezone. You can:
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/scheduling.boundary: Published items show when they ran and cannot be moved.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/settings.audience: Use this tab when the setting should differ between brands, clients, or projects.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/settings.boundary: The media lifecycle information is not a workspace control.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/threads.audience: This page is for people creating ordered multi-post sequences.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/threads.boundary: Failures in early posts can block later posts in the same thread.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/video-edito.audience: OpenPost Video Editor is a local-first multitrack editor for social video.
https://docs.openpo.st/usage/video-edito.boundary: Editing, rendering, and transcription run on the device. Cloud Video Projects synchronize authored state and required originals, but OpenPost does not provide server rendering or a server transcription fallback.

https://docs.openpo.st/usage/workspaces.audience: Use a workspace to keep one brand, client, or project separate.

https://docs.openpo.st/configuration/.audience: Use this page when configuring a self-hosted deployment or the Hosted service.
https://docs.openpo.st/configuration/.boundary: Use the linked references for complete environment-variable and provider-application details.

https://docs.openpo.st/configuration/inv.audience: This page is for operators integrating an email provider's delivery callbacks.
https://docs.openpo.st/configuration/inv.boundary: A successful delivery job marks a Workspace invitation Sent.

https://docs.openpo.st/operations/provid.audience: This page is for operators and release reviewers deciding whether a provider-format claim is current.
https://docs.openpo.st/operations/provid.boundary: OpenPost keeps provider implementation, setup, evidence, approval, and runtime control as separate facts. An adapter in the binary proves only that code exists. It does not make a provider or format ready, connectable, publishable, or safe to advertise.

https://docs.openpo.st/providers/.audience: OAuth and social app setup cause many connection errors. Use this guide as you turn on each network.
